title: Z.ai Confirms Development of Ox Alpha Open Source Model Weights Will Be Released and Added to the GLM Series

content_html:
Zhipu recently confirmed that the anonymous open-source model Ox Alpha, which has attracted attention from developers on OpenRouter recently, was developed by them. This model is the latest version of the GLM series. Previously, Ox Alpha was launched on OpenRouter under the name of the anonymous "Stealth" model and achieved outstanding performance in various benchmark tests and rankings, sparking widespread speculation within the community about its developer.

Zhipu stated that the model weights of Ox Alpha will be made available on Wednesday, allowing developers to conduct secondary development based on this model. The model is positioned as a reasoning model for coding, continuous intelligence work, and production environment tasks, mainly used for long-term software engineering, complex reasoning, and multimodal workflows that combine text and visual contexts.

According to the introduction, Ox Alpha maintains technical connections with the previous GLM series models from Z.ai. This series of models has also been used in related AI security testing scenarios recently, and Hugging Face successfully defended against attacks from OpenAI agents using the GLM series models. The public disclosure of Ox Alpha's identity also means that Z.ai is further expanding its open-source model ecosystem.

The emergence of Ox Alpha further highlights the competitiveness of Chinese AI companies in the field of open-source large models. In recent years, manufacturers such as Z.ai and DeepSeek have continuously released low-cost, high-performance models, forming new competitive pressure on overseas closed-source model vendors like OpenAI and Anthropic. Early this month, Z.ai also released GLM-5.3, which has approached the level of international leading models in some benchmark tests.

As the capabilities of open-source models continue to improve, competition in the AI industry is shifting from simply pursuing model parameter scale to a comprehensive comparison of reasoning capabilities, developer ecosystems, cost efficiency, and practical application deployment capabilities.
